note: LY500307 (erteberel) involuted the mouse prostate without touching hormones, but in 414 BPH patients it shrank nothing; a second ERβ agonist, S-equol, was null on the registry too.
label: BPH (ERβ agonists)

engagement.note: ERβ-null (BERKO) mouse prostate grows hyperplastic foci with raised AR; the target-biology model behind the class.
engagement.quote: In prostates from mice in which the ERbeta gene has been inactivated (BERKO), androgen receptor (AR) levels are elevated, and the tissue contains multiple hyperplastic foci.
engagement.judgement: Genetic model, no drug dosed: it defines the target (ERβ restrains epithelial growth, raises AR when absent) rather than testing an agonist. Opens the strip because this paper is what proposed ERβ-selective ligands for BPH. Quote from the PNAS abstract (PMC33468).

engagement.model: Human BPH tissue xenografts dosed with 8β-VE2
engagement.note: 8β-VE2 drove apoptosis in xenografted human BPH tissue; no ERβ-engagement readout was ever taken in a patient's prostate.
engagement.short: ERβ agonist kills human BPH xenograft cells
engagement.quote: In human tissues, ERbeta agonist induces apoptosis in stroma and epithelium of xenografted BPH specimens, including in the CD133(+) enriched putative stem/progenitor cells isolated from BPH-1 cells in vitro.
engagement.judgement: Closest thing to an engagement model: apoptosis in human BPH stroma/epithelium with a class proxy (8β-VE2, never in the clinic), not LY500307. The LY500307 Phase 2 (NCT01097707, results posted 2019-04-08) measured PSA, prostate volume and testosterone only; no biopsy, apoptosis or ERβ-occupancy marker was taken, so engagement in patients was never compared. Abstract-level reading (PMC2840300 available).

dose.model: CD-1 mouse ventral prostate involution (SERBA-1 = LY500307)
dose.note: Mouse gave a 10× window between prostate-involuting and hormone-suppressing doses; no source ties patient exposure at 1–25 mg to it.
dose.short: Mouse 10× window never tied to patients
dose.quote: SERBA-1 in vivo demonstrates involution of the ventral prostate in CD-1 mice (ERbeta effect), while having no effect on gonadal hormone levels (ERalpha effect) at 10x the efficacious dose, consistent with in vitro properties of this molecule.
dose.reason: Mouse-efficacious exposure never checked in patients
dose.judgement: SERBA-1 is LY500307/erteberel (PubChem CID 10286159 lists SERBA-1, LY500307 and erteberel as synonyms), so the clinical product was dosed in the model. The human dose ceiling did not come from this model: Hu 2015 (doi:10.1002/cpdd.184, single doses 0.5–500 mg in 30 healthy men) set the top dose from total-testosterone suppression (Emax ~28.6%, EC50 ~1.69 ng/mL). Whether 1–25 mg/day reached the mouse prostate-involuting exposure is not published (Roehrborn 2015 full text paywalled; abstract gives no dose rationale). J Med Chem abstract only; the 'efficacious dose' value itself is not in the abstract.

efficacy.note: ERβ-null mice grow prostatic hyperplasia, so the authors proposed ERβ-specific ligands to manage BPH.
efficacy.quote: These findings suggest that ligands specific for ERbeta may be useful in the prevention and/or clinical management of prostatic hyperplasia and neoplasia.
efficacy.judgement: Loss-of-function prediction (no ERβ → hyperplasia) read as gain-of-function therapy (agonist → regression). Opens the strip; the drug-dosed model follows in 2006.

efficacy.model: CD-1 mouse ventral prostate involution (SERBA-1 = LY500307)
efficacy.note: LY500307 (SERBA-1) involuted the CD-1 mouse ventral prostate: the pivotal preclinical efficacy claim for the BPH programme.
efficacy.short: LY500307 shrinks the mouse ventral prostate
efficacy.quote: SERBA-1 in vivo demonstrates involution of the ventral prostate in CD-1 mice (ERbeta effect), while having no effect on gonadal hormone levels (ERalpha effect) at 10x the efficacious dose, consistent with in vitro properties of this molecule.
efficacy.judgement: Added as a model-change entry (status unchanged) because this, not the knockout, is the model the Lilly programme relied on; Hilbish 2013 (doi:10.1002/bdrb.21083) confirms LY500307 'was developed for the treatment of benign prostatic hyperplasia'. Note it is a normal intact mouse, not a hyperplastic prostate: involution of a healthy gland was the efficacy surrogate. Abstract only (J Med Chem letter, paywalled).

efficacy.model: CD-1 mouse ventral prostate involution (SERBA-1 = LY500307)
efficacy.note: LY500307 1–25 mg for 24 weeks shrank neither prostate volume nor IPSS in 414 men; Lilly stopped at the interim.
efficacy.short: No prostate shrinkage; Lilly stopped at interim
efficacy.quote: A total of 414 patients were randomized when the study was terminated because of insufficient TPV reduction, based on a priori defined interim analysis.
efficacy.reason: Mouse prostate shrank; patients' did not
efficacy.judgement: Why contra: the mouse predicted gland involution; the a-priori proof-of-concept endpoint in patients was total prostate volume, and the trial was stopped for insufficient TPV reduction. Registry NCT01097707 (Eli Lilly; whyStopped 'Terminated due to insufficient efficacy'; results first posted 2019-04-08): TPV % change at 24 wk 1 mg +1.6, 3 mg −4.5, 10 mg −6.7, 25 mg +1.3 vs placebo −6.6; IPSS change −1.3/−2.6/−3.7/−4.4 vs −3.4 (abstract: P>0.05); Qmax and PSA null. The abstract does not mention the mouse model, so the comparison is mine (comparison_stated false); full text is paywalled. A second class member, S-equol (AUS-131, Ausio; NCT00962390, 116 men, 4 weeks, results first posted 2017-05-19) was also null: PSA change vs placebo +0.3/+0.3/+0.1 ng/mL (p=0.47/0.49/0.82), prostate volume −3.0/−0.3/−1.7 vs −1.7 mL; never published (PubMed search found only a nutraceutical review). It does not change the status and is registry-only, so it is recorded here rather than as an entry. The manifest/caller hint NCT00407849 is a triamcinolone diabetic-macular-oedema trial, not LY500307.

safety.note: Mouse showed no gonadal-hormone (ERα) effect at 10× the prostate-involuting dose: the class's selectivity-window safety claim.
safety.quote: SERBA-1 in vivo demonstrates involution of the ventral prostate in CD-1 mice (ERbeta effect), while having no effect on gonadal hormone levels (ERalpha effect) at 10x the efficacious dose, consistent with in vitro properties of this molecule.
safety.judgement: The safety prediction is the ERα window: feminisation/testosterone suppression only when selectivity (32-fold ERβ over ERα in vitro, per Hilbish 2013 doi:10.1002/bdrb.21083) is exceeded. Hilbish 2013 (rat/rabbit fertility and embryo-fetal tox) later attributed reproductive-tissue atrophy at 10 mg/kg/day in male rats 'predominantly' to off-target ERα effects at parentally toxic doses; cited here rather than as a separate entry because the status does not change.

safety.note: No testosterone fall or feminisation signal at 1–25 mg; adverse events matched placebo, as the mouse hormone window predicted.
safety.short: Hormones untouched at 1–25 mg, as predicted
safety.quote: LY500307 was well tolerated in BPH patients with LUTS at doses up to 25 mg once daily for 24 weeks.
safety.reason: Clean hormones at therapeutic doses, as predicted
safety.judgement: Judgement call: 'same' because the model's specific prediction (ERβ-selective doses leave gonadal hormones alone) held in patients. Registry NCT01097707: fasting total testosterone change −12.5/−1.3/−24.9/+24.6 ng/dL vs placebo −14.6; gynecomastia 1/80 (3 mg), breast enlargement 1/82 (10 mg), breast tenderness 1/83 (1 mg), hot flush 1/83 (1 mg), serious AEs 2–4 per arm vs 3/85 placebo. The boundary of the window also matched: Hu 2015 (doi:10.1002/cpdd.184, 30 healthy men, single doses to 500 mg) states LY500307 'loses its selectivity at high dose and leads to undesirable suppression of total testosterone' (Emax ~28.6%, EC50 ~1.69 ng/mL), i.e. ERα effects appear above the window, as the mouse and in-vitro selectivity predicted. Caveat: the clean patient profile is partly by design, since the 25 mg ceiling was set below the healthy-volunteer testosterone threshold. Comparison is mine (abstract + registry; full text paywalled). Downgrade to 'untested' if the rules require the source itself to state the comparison.
